stamped reject on "Lightbox": Real pixels appear only on kitty-protocol terminals, so on Windows Terminal and most others the card falls back to a line of file names and sizes, which is a variation on changes-widget and activity-widget at twelve rows of height.

stamped reject on "Ports": Its cost is out of proportion: a netstat or lsof run plus loopback requests every few seconds, with no reliable way to tie a listener to this session, for a problem that turns up a few times a month.
stamped reject on "Upstream": A variation on git-widget's ahead and behind line that pays for itself with a background git fetch moving the person's remote-tracking refs every few minutes.

stamped reject on "Tired": A variation on mirror-widget and coffee-widget: a backspace ratio is too noisy to tell tiredness from editing a long prompt, so the one line it exists for would mostly be wrong.
stamped reject on "Duck": The same swallowed-draft idea as Unsent, rejected twice already: it still cannot tell a solved problem from a change of mind, as its own inventor says.
stamped reject on "Quote": Not chosen: ui.selection is real and unused, but it saves only a copy and a paste the terminal already offers, and it needs a mouse in the fullscreen layout to work at all.

stamped reject on "Aim": Not chosen: useful on the day it fires, but it is stakes-widget's line under the dialog fed from a different source, it is an empty card for anyone without kubectl, AWS or a database URL, and guessing which name means production will misfire.

stamped reject on "Chesterton": Not chosen: the strongest runner-up, but most edits replace lines the person or Claude wrote this week, so the card is noise until the rare old line, and a blame before every edit is paid for all of them.
named the widget squiggle-widget ("Squiggle")

stamped pass: The only idea that draws inside the prompt box as the person types, on the unused prompt.edit decorations: it stops the misnamed-file turn before it is sent, costs no tokens, and is narrowed to path-shaped words so it does not misfire.
